What to look for in adventure boots

  • Ankle protection. Rigid ankle cups and a torsion-control sole protect the joints most at risk in a fall.
  • Waterproof membrane. Your feet sit lowest on the bike — a Gore-Tex or equivalent liner is essential in the UK.
  • Walk test them. Touring means walking too — choose a sole flexible enough for castles, pubs and fuel stops.
  • Break them in. Wear new boots around the house and on short rides before committing to a big tour.

Frequently asked questions

How much should I spend on adventure boots?

Our catalogue spans £119.99 to £511.98. Budget options under £150 cover the essentials, the £150–£400 mid-range hits the sweet spot for most UK tourers, and premium picks above £400 add refinement, lighter materials and longer-term durability.

Which brands are worth considering?

Popular, well-reviewed brands in this category include Alpinestars, Klim, Eleveit, RST, Richa. All are stocked by SportsBikeShop with UK warranty support.

Do I really need waterproof kit?

In the UK, yes. Cold, wet hands and feet impair control and concentration within minutes. A waterproof membrane is one of the best touring upgrades you can make.

faq.a: If you ride mostly road with occasional trails, an adventure boot such as the Klim Adventure Gore-Tex or RST Adventure-X flexes to walk and stand on the pegs. Choose a stiffer enduro boot like the Tech 7 Enduro only if hard off-road riding dominates.

faq.q: Do adventure boots keep water out?
faq.a: The waterproof models do. Look for Gore-Tex, Drystar or Sinaqua linings, as on the Klim Adventure, Tech 7 Enduro Drystar and RST Adventure-X. Some off-road-focused boots are drainage-vented rather than sealed, so check the spec if dry feet matter.

faq.q: Can I walk and hike in adventure boots?
faq.a: Yes, that is a key design goal. Adventure boots use flex zones and grippier soles so you can walk around campsites, refuel and hike short distances. They will never match trainers, but they are far more walkable than dedicated race or motocross boots.

faq.q: How much protection do I lose versus an MX boot?
faq.a: A road-biased adventure boot flexes more at the ankle, so it offers slightly less rigid protection than a full motocross boot like the Tech 10 Enduro. For most UK green-laning and touring that is a sensible trade for comfort and all-day wearability.
